title: Customer on-prem Connectivity Risk Bucketing and Engagement Protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a standardized risk-bucketing framework and a prescriptive engagement protocol for handling customer requests for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments where networking constraints or air-gapped environments are the primary blockers. The outcome must enable fast, repeatable Triage -> Guidance -> Remediation paths and clear handoffs to SRE/Network/Account teams.
problem_statement: We receive a high volume of ad-hoc 'we want private deployment' requests that stall on diverse networking constraints (firewalls, proxy, egress policies, HSM/KMS, airgap). Lack of a consistent triage rubric increases time-to-onboard, escalations to engineering, and customer churn. Current intake lacks risk-first prioritization and templated remediation paths.
objectives: Define concise risk buckets (Low/Medium/High/Blocked) tied to measurable network signals and time-to-remediate SLAs
Ship an engagement protocol (self-serve probes, required artifacts, escalation lanes) for each bucket
Reduce average triage-to-commit time from request to scheduled deployment by 40% for Medium/High customers
Reduce engineering touch for Low-risk customers via self-serve remediation templates
success_metrics: Median triage time (first human response) <= 4 business hours
Triage-to-scheduled-deployment median reduced by 40% for Medium/High buckets within quarter
Percent of requests closed with self-serve guidance >= 25%
Number of escalations to core runtime engineers reduced by 30%
scope_inclusions: Intake form additions for network topology and constraints
Self-serve probe scripts and packaged network troubleshooting checklist
Customer comms templates for each bucket and SLA
Runbook & handoff checklist for SRE/Network/Account teams
scope_exclusions: Implementing new network proxies or agent code in customer environments
Replacing customer KMS/HSM integrations (we'll document compatibility requirements only)
Automated patching/upgrade orchestration for customer infra (out of scope for this ticket)
acceptance_criteria: Published risk bucketing rubric (doc + decision table) in Confluence
Intake form updated in Support portal and internal triage UI with required fields
Set of probe scripts (curl, traceroute, small client) published in Drive with usage guide
Customer comms templates checked into repo and available from the triage UI
SRE and Account teams have a 1-hour workshop and sign-off on handoff checklist
proposed_flow_steps: 1) New request ingested via intake form -> automatic preliminary bucket based on required fields
2) System-run lightweight probes (optional customer opt-in) produce a readiness report
3) Triage owner reviews readiness report and confirms bucket: Low/Medium/High/Blocked

4) Auto-send customer comms with specific remediation path and SLA. For Low: self-serve checklist. For Medium: scheduled self-service session with Solutions. For High: Engineer-assisted remediation lane with runbook. For Blocked: Legal/Compliance + Sales escalation
5) Handoff via standardized ticket to SRE/Network with prefilled artifacts and recommended schedule
6) Post-deployment checklist and telemetry hooks to validate connectivity and performance
risk_buckets: Low: Standard VPC with internet egress allowed, customer can run probe scripts; expected remediation < 3 business days
Medium: VPC with restrictive egress or proxy; customer needs network team coordination; expected remediation 3-14 business days
High: Airgap or only private peering with mandatory legal/ops approvals; requires scheduled engineering work and controlled transport of artifacts; expected remediation 2-8 weeks
Blocked: Unsupported OS/old network hardware, missing required compliance (e.g., no HSM available), or customer refuses minimal outbound telemetry; requires executive review
decision_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: prefer self-serve probes (faster) vs privacy concerns (some customers disallow any internet probes). Mitigation: make probes opt-in and provide offline checklists for airgapped customers.
Tradeoff: automated bucketing reduces manual work but risks false positives. Mitigation: keep human-in-loop and show confidence score on bucket recommendation.
Tradeoff: more stringent required intake fields improve triage quality but add friction to signup. Mitigation: progressive disclosure of fields depending on initial answers.
stakeholder_feedback: Solutions Eng requested a handoff payload that includes traceroute, proxy headers, and KMS type to avoid back-and-forth (Action: include these fields in intake)
Legal emphasized need for a template DPIA note for customers in EU airgap scenarios
SRE asked for a minimum set of telemetry hooks post-install (latency pings, TLS handshake logs) and asked that data retention be configurable per customer
operational_runbooks: Preflight checklist (customer-facing) - includes required certs, IP allowlists, KMS metadata
Engineer remediation runbook - step-by-step for Medium and High buckets
Rollback checklist and emergency contact matrix
communications_templates: Low bucket email: templated self-serve steps + link to probe script
Medium bucket email: proposed appointment times + link to shared debugging session template
High bucket email: executive summary + expected timeline + legal/ops preflight required items
Blocked bucket escalation note: list of blocking items and next escalation owner
